chapter_title_ka: წიგნი ტარიელისა ინდოეთ მეფის წინაშე და გამარჯვებით შემოქცევა
chapter_title_en: Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return
chapter_expert_explanation_en: Tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
წიგნი დავწერე: “მეფეო, სვემცა არს თქვენი სვიანად!
მე ხატაელთა მიმუხთლეს, თუცა მათ ეცა ზიანად;
ჩემი ამბავი დასტური ამად გაცნობე გვიანად,
და მეფე შევიპყარ, მოგივალ მე ალაფიან–ტყვიანად”.
stanzas.english_translation: "I wrote a letter: 'O king, great is your good fortune! The Khatavians plotted treachery to me, though it fell on them to their hurt; therefore am I tardy in telling you my true tidings. I have captured the king; I come to thee with spoil and prisoners.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 463; Wardrop Stanza 448): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“რა ყველაი დავიურვე, ხატაეთით გავემგზავრე,
წამოვიხვენ საჭურჭლენი, სახელმწიფო დავიავრე,
ვერ მოვეყავ აქლემითა, აზავრები ვააზავრე,
და მოვირჭვენ და მოვივლინე, რაცა მწადდა, აგრე ვყავ-რე.
stanzas.english_translation: "When I had put everything in order I set out from Khataet’hi. I took the treasures, I despoiled the kingdom, I could not get enough camels, I loaded bullocks with the burdens; I had found glory and honour, for what I had desired that had I obtained.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 464; Wardrop Stanza 449): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ხატაეთისა ხელმწიფე მომყვანდა შეპყრობილია.
ინდოეთს მივე, მეგება ჩემი გამზრდელი ტკბილია;
რა ქება მითხრა, არ ითქმის, ჩემგან სათქმელად წბილია,
და ხელი გამიხსნა, შემომკრა მან სახვეველი ლბილია.
stanzas.english_translation: "I led away captive the King of Khataet’hi. I came to India, sweet was the meeting with my foster-father; what eulogy he uttered to me cannot be repeated, for me to tell it were unseemly; he undid mine arm, he bound it with a soft bandage.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 465; Wardrop Stanza 450): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ედგნეს ტურფანი კარავნი მოედანს ჩამოდგომილსა,
საუბრისა და ჭვრეტისა ჩემისა მას მონდომილსა.
მას დღესა ედვა ნადიმი მას შიგან გარდახდომილსა;
და მიალერსებდა, მიჭვრეტდა წინაშე ახლოს ჯდომილსა.
stanzas.english_translation: "Fair tents stood pitched in the public square (maidan) for him who desired to speak with and gaze upon me. That day he (the king) who rested there spread a banquet, he caressed me, sitting near me he gazed at me.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 466; Wardrop Stanza 451): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მას ღამით ვსხედით ნადიმად, მუნ ამოდ გავიხარენით,
დილასა ქალაქს შევედით, მოედნით ავიყარენით;
მეფემან ბრძანა: «ლაშქარნი უხმენით, შემოჯარენით,
და დღეს ხატაელი მიჩვენეთ, ტყვენიცა შემომგვარენით”.
stanzas.english_translation: "That night we spent in feasting; pleasantly we made merry there. In the morning we left the maidan; we entered the city. The king commanded: 'Call the soldiers, assemble them, show me this day the Khatavians, lead in the prisoners.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 467; Wardrop Stanza 452): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“რამაზ მეფე მას წინაშე შეპყრობილი მოვიყვანე;
ტკბილად ნახა ხელმწიფემან, ვითა შვილი სააკვანე.
ორგული და მოღალატე ნამსახურსა დავამგვანე,
და ესე არის მამაცისა მეტის-მეტი სიგულვანე.
stanzas.english_translation: "I led in King Ramaz captive before him. The king looked sweetly on him as on a son whom he had cradled. I made the deceitful and treacherous one seem deserving, and this is the excess of heroism in a brave man.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 468; Wardrop Stanza 453): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მას მეფესა ხატაელსა უმასპინძლა, უალერსა,
ჟამიერად უბრძანებდის საუბარსა მათსა ფერსა.
ცისკრად მიხმეს, მიბრძანებდეს მე სიტყვასა ლმობიერსა:
და «შეუნდობო ხატაელსა, მას აქამდის შენამტერსა?”
stanzas.english_translation: "He entertained the King of the Khatavians, he caressed him, he conversed with him for a long time in a fitting manner; at dawn I was called, he spoke to me a compassionate word: 'Shall I pardon the Khatavian, my former enemy?'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 469; Wardrop Stanza 454): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე ვჰკადრე: «ღმერთი ვინათგან შეუნდობს შეცოდებულსა,
უყავით თქვენცა წყალობა მას ღონე-გაცუდებულსა”.
რამაზს უბრძანებს: «იცოდი, გაგგზავნი შეწყალებულსა,
და მაგრა ნუ გნახავთ კვლაცაღა ჩვენს წინა გაწბილებულსა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "I ventured to reply: 'Since God forgives the sinner, be you also merciful to him whose might is brought to nought.' He said to Ramaz: 'Know that I send thee hence forgiven, but show not thyself before me again disgraced.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 470; Wardrop Stanza 455): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ხარაჯა დასდვეს, შეჰკვეთეს დრაჰკანი ასჯერ ასია,
კვლა ხატაური მრავალი, სხვა სტავრა, სხვა ატლასია.
მერმე ყველანი დამოსა იგი და მისი ხასია,
და შეწყალებული გაგზავნა, უყო რისხვისა ფასია.
stanzas.english_translation: "He levied a tribute of a hundred times a hundred drachmas, also a thousand khatauris, also brocades and satins; then he clad him and all his courtiers, and sent them away with pardon in place of wrath.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 471; Wardrop Stanza 456): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ხატაელმან დაუმადლა, დადრკა, მდაბლად ეთაყვანა;
მოახსენა: «ორგულობა თქვენი ღმერთმან შემანანა.
თუღა ოდეს შეღაგცოდო, მაშინ მომკალ მეცა განა!”
და წავიდა და ყველაკაი მისი თანა წაიტანა.
stanzas.english_translation: "The Khatavian thanked him, bent, paid lowly homage; he said: 'By God, I repent my treachery towards you; if ever I sin against you again then kill me.' He departed and took all his (folk) with him.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 472; Wardrop Stanza 457): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მოვიდა კაცი მეფისა, ცისკრობს, არ დანაღამია,
ებრძანა: «შენგან გაყრილვარ მას აქათ თვეო სამია,
მინდორს მოკლული ისრითა ნადირი არ მიჭამია,
და არ დამაშვრალხარ, წამოდი, თუცა დაშვრომის ჟამია”.
stanzas.english_translation: "A man of the king's came; it was dawn, and the morning grey was past; he brought a message: 'For three months have I been separated from thee, I have eaten no game killed by arrow in the field; if thou be not tired come forth, though it be time to be tired.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 473; Wardrop Stanza 458): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“შევეკაზმე, დარბაზს მივე, დამხვდა ჯარი ავაზისა,
შავარდნითა სავსე იყო სრულად არე დარბაზისა,
მეფე ქვე ჯდა შეკაზმული, შვენებითა მსგავსი მზისა;
და გაეხარნეს მისვლა ჩემი ტურფისა და ლამაზისა!
stanzas.english_translation: "I apparelled myself, I went into the hall of audience; a pack of harriers met me, all the space round the hall was full of falcons. The king sat decked in beauty like the sun; he rejoiced at the coming of me, the lovely and fair.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 474; Wardrop Stanza 459): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“იდუმალ ცოლსა ეუბნა, მართ ჩემგან უცოდნელია:
«ომით მოსრული ტარიელ საჭვრეტად სასურველია,
მან განანათლოს ჭვრეტელთა გული, რაზომცა ბნელია:
და რაცა დაგვედრო საქმნელად, ქმენ, არა საზოზღნელია.
stanzas.english_translation: "He said secretly to his wife, but unknown to me To gaze on Tariel returned from war is desirable, he brings light to the onlooker's heart, however dark it may be; whatever I ask thee to do, do it without delay.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 475; Wardrop Stanza 460): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
«აწ მითქვამს საქმე უშენოდ, შენცა ცან ესე მცნებული;
რათგან ქალია სამეფოდ ჩვენგანვე სახელ-დებული,
ვინცაღა ნახავს, აწ ნახოს, აჰა დღე, ედემს ხლებული,
და გვერდსა დაისვი, ორნივე სრას დამხვდით, მოვალ შვებული”.
stanzas.english_translation: "'Now, without (consulting) thee I have thought of a plan; but thou too must know it: Since the maid is to be king, and has been so nominated by us ourselves, whoever shall see her, now let him who is like a tree in Eden see her--lo! even to-day; seat her by thy side, both of you meet us in the palace, I shall come joyful.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 476; Wardrop Stanza 461): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.english_translation: "We hunted over plain, mountain-foot and hill; there was a multitude of hounds, falcons and hawks. We returned early without having gone a stage from the long road. They did not play at ball; they broke up two games.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 477; Wardrop Stanza 462): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ჩემთა მჭვრეტელთა მოეცვა ქალაქი, შუკა და ბანი.
ომ-გარდახდილსა მშვენოდეს მე ენიანნი კაბანი;
ფერმიხდილ-გვარად ვშვენოდი ვარდი, ცრემლითა ნაბანი,
და ვინცა მიჭვრეტდის, ბნდებოდის, - მათრლად არს, არ კატაბანი.
stanzas.english_translation: "Folk eager to gaze on me filled the city, the bazaar and the roofs; tasselled robes adorned me who had finished the war; I was fair as a pale-hued rose bathed in tears, he who looked on me fainted; true is this, and no falsehood.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 478; Wardrop Stanza 463): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“რიდენი რომე მეშოვნეს ქალაქსა ხატაელთასა,
იგი მეხვივნეს, მშვენოდეს, ვახელებ გულსა ხელთასა.
მეფე გარდახდა, დარბაზსა შევედით ჩემთა მზრდელთასა,
და შევხედენ, დავჰკრთი ელვასა ღაწვთა მზეებრ ნათელთასა.
stanzas.english_translation: "The veils I had found in the city of the Khatavians I bound round me, they became me, I maddened (still more) the heart of the mad. The king dismounted; we entered the apartments of my foster-parents. I saw the flash of her cheeks like sunlight, I trembled.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 479; Wardrop Stanza 464): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მას მზესა ტანსა ემოსნეს ნარინჯის-ფერნი ჯუბანი,
ზურგით უთქს ჯარი ხადუმთა, დას-დასად, უბან-უბანი.
სრულად ნათლითა აევსო სახლი, შუკა და უბანი,
და მუნ ვარდსა შუა შვენოდეს ძოწ-მარგალიტნი ტყუბანი.
stanzas.english_translation: "The form of that sun (Nestan) was clad in robes of orange; behind her was a host of eunuchs in cohorts and lines; with light she quite filled house, street and quarter; there, amid the roses (of her cheeks), shone in beauty coral-pearl twins (lips and rows of teeth).
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 480; Wardrop Stanza 465): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ნაომარსა, დაკოდილსა ხელი ყელსა ჩამომება.
დედოფალი საჯდომთაგან ადგა, წინა მომეგება,
ვითა შვილი გარდამკოცნა, ღაწვი ვარდი დამილება;
და მითხრა: «ნუ ეჭვ ამას იქით, თუღა მტერი შეღაგება”.
stanzas.english_translation: "I who had fought and been wounded had mine arm hung from my neck in a sling. The queen rose from her throne (and came) forward to meet me. She kissed me hard like a son, she made my rose cheek blue; she said to me: Henceforth expect not the foe to engage thee.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 481; Wardrop Stanza 466): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“ახლოს დამისვეს ადგილსა, მუნ, სადა მიამებოდა.
პირის-პირ მიჯდა იგი მზე, გული ვისთვისცა კვდებოდა.
მალვით ვუჭვრეტდი, მიჭვრეტდა, სხვად არად მეუბნებოდა”.
და თვალნი მოვსწყვიდნი, სიცოცხლე ამითა მეარმებოდა.
stanzas.english_translation: "Near at hand they made place for me, there where it pleased me; opposite sat the sun for whom my heart was dying. Stealthily I looked at her, she looked at me; no other converse was there; (when) I tore away mine eyes from her, thereby was life made hateful to me.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 482; Wardrop Stanza 467): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.english_translation: "There was drinking and feasting on a scale fitting to their might, such another rejoicing eye has not seen, goblet and cup were all of turquoise and ruby; the king gave order that no drunk man be suffered to depart.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 483; Wardrop Stanza 468): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“მე მუნა მყოფი მივეცი შვებასა მეტის-მეტასა.
არ შემომხედნის, შევხედნი, ცეცხლმან დამიწყის შრეტასა;
კაცთა კრძალვასა ვაწვევდი გულსა შმაგსა და რეტასა,
და რა უამეა პირის-პირ საყვარელისა ჭვრეტასა?!
stanzas.english_translation: "Being there I gave myself up to the excess of joy; when she gazed at me and I at her, my fire began to be extinguished. I called upon my wild, mad heart to have a care of men (that they observe not). How exceedingly pleasant it is to look face to face on the beloved!
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 484; Wardrop Stanza 469): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“დააგდეს მღერა მუტრიფთა, «სულეთო!” თავი ხარიან,
მიბრძანეს: «შვილო ტარიელ, ვით გითხრათ, ვით გვიხარიან;
ნეტარძი გვაქვსო, მებრძოლნი მით ჩვენნი ვაგლახ არიან,
და მართალან შენნი მჭვრეტელნი, არ ცუდად იმკვეხარიან!
stanzas.english_translation: "The minstrels ceased to sing. 'Be silent!' They bent their heads. He (the king) said to me: 'Son Tariel, how can we tell thee how we rejoice! We are in bliss, therefore (? because) our adversaries are woeful; right are thine admirers, not idly do they vaunt.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 485; Wardrop Stanza 470): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
«აწ თუცა გმართებს შემოსვა, ვის მორჭმით მოგივლენიან,
არ შეგმოსთ, მაგა კაბათა არ აგხდით,- ტურფად გშვენიან;
აწ გქონდეს ასი საჭურჭლე, ვის შუქნი მოგიფენიან,
და თვით შეიკერე, რაცა გწადს, ჩვენგან ნუღარა გრცხვენიან”.
stanzas.english_translation: "Now, though it is fitting that we should clothe thee who art mighty in glory, we clothe thee not, we doff not those robes beauteously adorning thee. Now thou whose rays are spread abroad hast a hundred treasures from us, thou thyself canst have sewn what thou desirest, be not bashful before us.'
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 486; Wardrop Stanza 471): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.english_translation: "He sat down again joyful, drinking and singing increased, again the feast went on, the lyres and tinkling of harps. The queens retired when day met twilight and until evenings joy was not joy.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 487; Wardrop Stanza 472): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“კვლაცა დაჯდა მხიარული, მოიმატა სმა და მღერა;
კვლა გაგრძელდა ნადიმობა, ბარბითი და ჩანგთა ჟღერა.
დედოფალი წამოვიდა, შეეყარა მწუხრსა დღე რა,
და ძილ-პირამდის სიხარულსა სიხარული ჰგვანდა ვერა.
stanzas.english_translation: "We broke up; we could no more endure the drinking of great goblets. I went into my chamber, my perception became like that of one dazed; I had no power in me, made prisoner as I was, to extinguish that fire (of love). I remembered, and the memory of being gazed on by her rejoiced me.
stanzas.expert_explanation_en: Chapter 19 ('Letter of Tariel to the King of the Indians and Triumphant Return', Stanza 488; Wardrop Stanza 473): Part of the narrative sequence in which tariel writes a victory dispatch to King Parsadan, returns in triumph to India, persuades Parsadan to show royal clemency to the captive King Ramaz upon payment of tribute, and sits opposite Nestan-Darejan at the victory banquet wearing the Khatavian veil she admired.

stanzas.georgian_raw_text:
“აიყარენით, მიგვჭირდა სმა დოსტაქნისა მეტისა.
საწოლს შემოვე, შემექმნა ცნობა მართ ვითა რეტისა.
ძალი არ მქონდა ტყვე-ქმნილსა მე ამა ცეცხლთა შრეტისა.
და მეგონებოდის, მალხენდის გონება მისგან ჭვრეტისა”.
stanzas.english_translation: "A slave came; he told me true tidings: 'A veiled woman asks tidings of you.' Then I knew at once, I leaped up in all haste, with trembling heart; she came in, I saw Asmat’h, who was coming towards me.

act_title: Act II: Tariel's Chronicle of India, Love & Loss

location.desc: Tributary realm of King Ramaz, subdued by Tariel in his heroic campaign.

key_maxim_en: Better a glorious death than a shameful life!
